306/2025.title: Transport Forum item 2: further consultation
306/2025.description: Item 2 from the November 2025 Local Transport Forum was deferred for more resident consultation.
306/2025.decisionSummary: Council deferred item 2 from the Local Transport Forum for further consultation with residents.

303/2025.title: Pottery Green Oval drainage budget
303/2025.description: Drainage works at Pottery Green Oval are being considered through Council's annual budget process.
303/2025.decisionSummary: Council agreed to consider Pottery Green Oval drainage works when preparing the 2026/27 Operational Plan and Budget.

301/2025.title: Ventemans Reach boardwalk tender
301/2025.description: The boardwalk and contaminated land remediation project requires a contractor within the available budget.
301/2025.decisionSummary: Council rejected all tenders because they substantially exceeded the budget. It authorised negotiations with preferred tenderers or another provider rather than calling fresh tenders.

298/2025.title: Pride celebration grants
298/2025.description: The pilot grant program supports public Pride celebrations run by Lane Cove businesses and not-for-profit organisations.
298/2025.decisionSummary: Council agreed to extend the pilot to all Lane Cove businesses and not-for-profit organisations for Pride celebrations. It required 28 days' public notice and applications to return to Council for a final decision.

295/2025.title: Councillors at the 2026 ALGWA conference
295/2025.description: Six councillors sought approval to attend the 2026 Australian Local Government Women's Association conference in Blacktown.
295/2025.decisionSummary: Council approved attendance by Councillors Southwood, Little, Flood, Kennedy, Greenwell and Bryla at the 2026 NSW ALGWA conference. Each councillor is to advise the General Manager of their preferred attendance days.

291/2025.title: Local government regulation review submission
291/2025.description: Council is responding to the NSW review of the Local Government General Regulation.
291/2025.decisionSummary: Council endorsed its submission to the Office of Local Government, subject to adding a safeguard that keeps the existing regulation in force until all stages of the review are complete.

289/2025.short: Canberra Avenue and Holdsworth planning agreement works
289/2025.title: Canberra Avenue and Holdsworth planning agreement works
289/2025.description: A proposed planning agreement variation changes the works and payments required from Silver Pond Investments at St Leonards South.
289/2025.decisionSummary: Council authorised negotiations and documents to reduce the Canberra and Holdsworth works and require the developer to pay the full monetary contributions. If the variation is executed and payment received, the offset funds must be retained for the specified works; councillors are to receive a February 2026 update on Holdsworth Pocket Park discussions.

284/2025.short: Sports field access for local clubs
284/2025.title: Sports field access for local clubs
284/2025.description: Council is reviewing whether sportsground hire arrangements meet the needs of clubs associated with Lane Cove.
284/2025.decisionSummary: Council requested a review of the Sportsground Hire Management Directive, including two years of bookings, local club needs and other councils' practices. Recommended changes are to return to Council in a report.

282/2025.title: Community safety and CCTV mapping
282/2025.description: Proposed safety work includes mapping CCTV locations and developing local activities with Police and Neighbourhood Watch.
282/2025.decisionSummary: Council requested a community safety camera mapping project, promotion of the NSW Police CCTV register and a program developed with Police, Neighbourhood Watch and other organisations. Programming and funding are to be considered in the 2026/27 budget.

278/2025.title: LGNSW board election congratulations
278/2025.description: Council recognised the elected Local Government NSW board, including Lane Cove Councillor Kathy Bryla.
278/2025.decisionSummary: Council congratulated the successful LGNSW board candidates and noted Councillor Kathy Bryla's election to the board.

272/2025.short: Greenwich New Year's Eve road closures
272/2025.title: Greenwich New Year's Eve road closures
272/2025.description: Traffic management plans cover road closures on the Greenwich Peninsula for New Year's Eve 2025.
272/2025.decisionSummary: Council approved the traffic management and traffic control plans for the 2025 New Year's Eve road closures in Greenwich Peninsula.

270/2025.title: Local Environmental Plan review
270/2025.description: Council's planning review covers proposed zoning rules, affordable housing, a potential Lane Cove North shop and possible additional property protections.
270/2025.decisionSummary: Council endorsed sending the revised planning proposal and draft clauses to the Department of Planning for Gateway determination. It also requested an affordable housing policy, a report on a possible Lane Cove North shop, and assessment of properties identified by the Bushland Management Advisory Committee, including 42a Ronald Street.

265/2025.short: Legal services panel and in-house counsel
265/2025.title: Legal services panel and in-house counsel
265/2025.description: Council is appointing external legal firms and investigating an in-house lawyer.
265/2025.decisionSummary: Council appointed Wilshire Webb Staunton Beattie, Marsdens Legal and HWL Ebsworth to its legal services panel for up to five years. It requested a February 2026 report on in-house legal counsel and authorised negotiations to extend Schmidt-Liermann's existing contract to no later than 30 December 2026.

258/2025.title: Pottery Green drainage proposal deferred
258/2025.description: Council sought club funding offers and contractor costs before considering proposed Pottery Green drainage works.
258/2025.decisionSummary: Council deferred the drainage proposal to December 2025. It requested written contribution offers from the sporting clubs and staff advice on contractor availability over Christmas and the total project cost.

252/2025.short: Galuwa roof solar and battery study
252/2025.title: Galuwa roof solar and battery study
252/2025.description: A proposed study would assess large-scale solar generation and optional batteries at Galuwa Sport and Recreation Centre.
252/2025.decisionSummary: Council requested a study of the roof's solar capacity, delivery options, costs, funding and community benefits, plus requests for state and federal support. Consultant funding is to be considered in the 2026/27 budget, with work starting in July 2026 and a report due in February 2027.

239/2025.short: Proposed Civic Centre piano hire fees
239/2025.title: Proposed Civic Centre piano hire fees
239/2025.description: Council proposed hourly hire fees for the Civic Centre concert grand piano.
239/2025.decisionSummary: Council proposed piano hire fees of $40 an hour for commercial use and $10 an hour for community or individual use. It required 28 days' public exhibition and a further report on submissions.

224/2025.short: Market Square lift and escalator failures
224/2025.title: Market Square lift and escalator failures
224/2025.description: Repeated lift, escalator and travelator failures at Market Square affect access and safety.
224/2025.decisionSummary: Council requested urgent discussions with Region Group, Knight Frank and other stakeholders to obtain the audit findings, identify causes and secure an improvement plan. A December 2025 report was requested, alongside better outage signage, repair estimates and alternative access information.

220/2025.short: Construction dust, noise and worker parking
220/2025.title: Construction dust, noise and worker parking
220/2025.description: Council is seeking stronger controls on construction dust, noise and worker parking near development sites.
220/2025.decisionSummary: Council requested development consent conditions for dust and noise monitoring and reporting, and parking plans for workers on major developments. Staff are to investigate monitoring equipment costs for the 2026/27 budget and seek similar conditions on relevant state significant developments.

218/2025.title: Spanish moss near bushland
218/2025.description: Council is considering mapping and removing Spanish moss from street trees near local bushland.
218/2025.decisionSummary: Council requested consideration of 2026/27 funding to map Spanish moss near bushland, prepare a removal plan and accelerate removal. It also agreed to advocate for priority weed classification to allow enforcement under biosecurity law.

198/2025.short: Longer library and community facility hours
198/2025.title: Longer library and community facility hours
198/2025.description: Council is considering longer opening hours and possible 24-hour library access.
198/2025.decisionSummary: Council agreed to consider extended library and Council-owned community facility hours at its planning weekend and during 2026/27 budget preparation, including exploring 24-hour access options.

185/2025.title: Food scraps collection rollout
185/2025.description: A separate food-only bin service is planned for houses, followed by an opt-in service for other dwellings.
185/2025.decisionSummary: Council approved a fifth, food-only bin under existing contracts, targeting a March 2026 start while keeping other services. It requested an implementation report six months after the house rollout and before the opt-in service for other dwellings, followed by investigation of further waste service improvements.

176/2025.title: 170 Pacific Highway planning agreement
176/2025.description: A proposed planning agreement relates to development at 170 Pacific Highway, Greenwich.
176/2025.decisionSummary: Council agreed to publicly exhibit the draft planning agreement and supporting documents for 170 Pacific Highway, Greenwich, and receive a report on the results.

159/2025.short: St Leonards South development contributions review
159/2025.title: St Leonards South development contributions review
159/2025.description: Council is reviewing the St Leonards South plan for developer contributions to local infrastructure.
159/2025.decisionSummary: Council noted the exhibition results and that Appendix B was unchanged from the plan adopted in April 2022. It authorised the General Manager to submit the draft 2025 contributions plan, including Appendix B.

155/2025.short: Proposed Anglo Road closure and sale
155/2025.title: Proposed Anglo Road closure and sale
155/2025.description: The proposed sale of Anglo Road in St Leonards requires a road closure process and development consent.
155/2025.decisionSummary: Council authorised sale negotiations and the road closure process. Community consultation results must return to Council before any sale is finalised, and any sale agreement must be conditional on the relevant development application receiving consent.

138/2025.title: Councillor and staff interaction policy
138/2025.description: The policy sets rules for how councillors and Council staff work with one another.
138/2025.decisionSummary: Council adopted the revised interaction policy, noted that supporting guidelines would be developed, and agreed that proposed performance measures would appear in the Council Snapshot every six months.

54/2025.short: Stringybark Creek and Burns Bay water catchments
54/2025.title: Stringybark Creek and Burns Bay water catchments
54/2025.description: Council is investigating catchment plans, cleaner waterways and water reuse for Stringybark Creek and Burns Bay Reserve.
54/2025.decisionSummary: Council requested a report on the resources and funding needed for catchment plans, including water quality and runoff targets, methods and timelines. It also requested Sydney Water and stakeholder discussions, community education on water management and investigation of bioswales through the On the Verge program.

255/2024.short: Central Ward traffic safety and 40 km/h study
255/2024.title: Central Ward traffic safety and 40 km/h study
255/2024.description: A proposed Central Ward traffic study would examine safety and possible 40 km/h limits, including Finlayson Street.
255/2024.decisionSummary: Council requested community engagement and a report on the cost of a traffic safety study aimed at reducing speed limits to 40 km/h. It required the project to be included in strategic planning and considered for the 2025/26 program and budget, alongside River Road West safety work.

251/2024.short: Climate emergency plan and emissions targets
251/2024.title: Climate emergency plan and emissions targets
251/2024.description: Council is reviewing its climate plan and emissions targets for its operations and the wider Lane Cove area.
251/2024.decisionSummary: Council requested a Climate Emergency Plan, an administration net-zero target of 2028 and an aspirational community target of 2040. It also requested assessment of extra resources, a dedicated website page and options for showing how Council decisions address climate, equity, cost and other considerations.

158/2024.title: Community shuttle feasibility
158/2024.description: Council is investigating whether a local shuttle service could connect residential areas, shops, recreation areas and transport hubs.
158/2024.decisionSummary: Council requested preliminary investigation of routes, schedules, costs, funding and partnerships for a community e-shuttle or regular shuttle bus. It also requested consideration of using aged care providers' buses for wider community services.

129/2023.short: St Leonards South areas 13–15 planning agreement
129/2023.title: St Leonards South areas 13–15 planning agreement
129/2023.description: The planning agreement covers development at Marshall Avenue, Holdsworth Avenue and Berry Road in St Leonards South.
129/2023.decisionSummary: Council agreed to enter a planning agreement for areas 13, 14 and 15 with Marshall Land and Holdsworth Land. It authorised the General Manager to review trustee assignment provisions, finalise the wording and sign the agreement.

34/2026.short: St Vincents Road shared path tender
34/2026.title: St Vincents Road shared path tender
34/2026.description: A shared walking and cycling path and associated road works are planned between Gore Street and Bob Campbell Oval.
34/2026.decisionSummary: Council accepted Solutions Plus Built's tender to construct the St Vincents Road shared user path and associated works. It authorised the General Manager to complete the necessary documents.

32/2026.title: Conflicts policy for Council development
32/2026.description: Council's policy addresses conflicts of interest when Council is involved in a development.
32/2026.decisionSummary: Council endorsed amendments to the policy for managing conflicts of interest in Council-related developments. It required public notification through its community engagement channels, including its website and newsletter.

29/2026.title: Lumen Lane road name proposal
29/2026.description: Council proposed Lumen Lane as the name for the new road between Park Road and Berry Road in St Leonards.
29/2026.decisionSummary: Council endorsed the name Lumen Lane and agreed to send the proposal to the NSW Geographical Names Board for consideration and approval.

27/2026.short: St Leonards South contributions plan adopted
27/2026.title: St Leonards South contributions plan adopted
27/2026.description: The amended contributions plan sets developer contributions for infrastructure in St Leonards South.
27/2026.decisionSummary: Council adopted the amended Section 7.11 Contributions Plan and required it to be published on its website as soon as practicable.

25/2026.title: Electric vehicle charging policy consultation
25/2026.description: The draft policy covers electric vehicle charging infrastructure.
25/2026.decisionSummary: Council agreed to exhibit the draft Electric Vehicle Charging Policy for 28 days and receive a report on the consultation results.

23/2026.title: Civic Centre piano hire program
23/2026.description: Council is establishing a hire program for the Civic Centre concert grand piano.
23/2026.decisionSummary: Council noted the consultation results, adopted the piano hire fees as exhibited and approved the start of the Piano Hire Program.

21/2026.short: Jean Mitchell Lucretia Baths foreshore rewilding
21/2026.title: Jean Mitchell Lucretia Baths foreshore rewilding
21/2026.description: Council is considering a different future for the baths site, which has been closed since February 2023.
21/2026.decisionSummary: Council endorsed foreshore rewilding as the revised direction for the site and requested funding in the 2026/27 budget. It also supported a heritage interpretation and oral history project.

19/2026.title: Councillor motions training
19/2026.description: Two councillors sought approval for training on managing motions and notices of motion.
19/2026.decisionSummary: Council approved Councillors Southwood and Greenwell attending the Local Government NSW training program, at $462 each from the Councillor Training Expenses Budget.

13/2026.title: December 2025 quarterly budget review
13/2026.description: Council reviewed its budget forecasts for the quarter ending December 2025.
13/2026.decisionSummary: Council noted the quarterly statements and approved revised forecasts: a $22 million operating surplus including capital grants and contributions, $55.9 million capital spending and a $13.4 million net reduction in transfers to and from reserves.

10/2026.title: In-house legal counsel position
10/2026.description: Council is creating an internal legal counsel role reporting to the General Manager.
10/2026.decisionSummary: Council allocated funding in the 2025/26 and future budgets for an in-house Legal Counsel position. It noted that a reduction in the Legal Services Budget would offset the additional salary costs.

8/2026.short: Donated phones for domestic violence survivors
8/2026.title: Donated phones for domestic violence survivors
8/2026.description: Council is investigating ways to collect donated mobile phones through DV Safe Phone alongside its existing ReConnect collection.
8/2026.decisionSummary: Council requested investigation of becoming a DV Safe Phone collection partner and donating retired Council phones. It also authorised work to encourage local businesses, schools and government agencies to donate decommissioned devices.

63/2026.title: February 2026 Local Transport Forum decisions
63/2026.description: Council considered the recommendations from the February Local Transport Forum meeting.
63/2026.decisionSummary: Council adopted the recommendations of the Local Transport Forum meeting held on 17 February 2026.

60/2026.title: NSW data centres inquiry submission
60/2026.description: Council is responding to a NSW inquiry about data centres, including their effects on power, water, noise and nearby bushland.
60/2026.decisionSummary: Council endorsed a submission calling for developers to fund supporting infrastructure, stronger generator and noise controls, protection of bushland and wildlife, and recycled water and renewable energy requirements. It authorised the General Manager to finalise and lodge the submission.

58/2026.title: Inclusive Communities Grants round 2
58/2026.description: Council considered funding applications under the extended Inclusive Communities Grant Program.
58/2026.decisionSummary: Council approved a $700 allocation under the Inclusive Communities Grant Program, as set out in the report attachment.

56/2026.title: 2026 local government national assembly attendance
56/2026.description: Seven councillors sought approval to attend the Australian Local Government Association's June 2026 national assembly.
56/2026.decisionSummary: Council approved attendance by Councillors Southwood, Roenfeldt, Kennedy, Flood, Little, Greenwell and Taylor, funded from the councillor training budget. The Mayor is the voting nominee, with Councillor Flood nominated if the Mayor is absent.

54/2026.title: 177–183 Greenwich Road planning agreement consultation
54/2026.description: A proposed planning agreement relates to development at 177–183 Greenwich Road, Greenwich.
54/2026.decisionSummary: Council agreed to publicly exhibit the draft planning agreement and supporting documents for 28 days and receive a report on the results.

51/2026.short: Gallery Lane Cove and Creative Studios funding
51/2026.title: Gallery Lane Cove and Creative Studios funding
51/2026.description: Council is considering financial support and future operating arrangements for Gallery Lane Cove and Creative Studios.
51/2026.decisionSummary: Council approved a $100,000 assistance package to stabilise operations and support a turnaround plan, with financial, marketing and program requirements. It agreed to work with the gallery board over six months on a sustainable funding model and seek further state and federal support.

47/2026.title: Walking and cycling infrastructure priorities
47/2026.description: Council is reviewing how to improve walking and cycling connections and align its transport plans.
47/2026.decisionSummary: Council supported reallocating road space for safe separated cycleways and reconfirmed that bike paths should not be built in bushland. It requested better alignment of walking and cycling plans, measurable infrastructure goals and requests for state and federal funding.

45/2026.title: Market Square building management review
45/2026.description: Council is seeking advice on building management, ownership responsibilities and unreliable lifts and escalators at Market Square.
45/2026.decisionSummary: Council expressed a lack of confidence in the current building management arrangements and requested advice on ownership, leases, contracts and Council's responsibilities. It requested a May or June report on management alternatives, legal options and repair or replacement costs.

42/2026.short: Reinstating Epping Road and Burns Bay Road bus stops
42/2026.title: Reinstating Epping Road and Burns Bay Road bus stops
42/2026.description: Council is seeking the return of bus stops removed near Fraser Street and Garthowen Avenue.
42/2026.decisionSummary: Council agreed to request urgent reinstatement of the Epping Road stop after Fraser Street and the Burns Bay Road stop at Garthowen Avenue. It also called for better bus services, supported returning the Region 7 network to public operation when feasible and authorised a media release.

84/2026.title: Infrastructure asset management consultation
84/2026.description: Council is consulting on its approach to managing infrastructure assets.
84/2026.decisionSummary: Council agreed to publicly exhibit the draft infrastructure asset management document and receive a report on the results.

82/2026.title: Small watercraft storage policy consultation
82/2026.description: The draft policy and fees cover storage of small watercraft on Council-managed land.
82/2026.decisionSummary: Council agreed to publicly exhibit the draft Small Watercraft Storage Policy and draft storage fees, with consultation results to return in a report.

80/2026.title: Sustainability Action Plan 2026–2030
80/2026.description: Council's sustainability plan sets its actions for 2026–2030 and reviews the previous plan's outcomes.
80/2026.decisionSummary: Council adopted the amended Sustainability Action Plan 2026–2030 and the outcomes report for the 2022–2025 plan.

78/2026.title: 94 Northwood Road heritage listing proposal
78/2026.description: A planning proposal sought to remove the heritage listing at 94 Northwood Road, Northwood.
78/2026.decisionSummary: Council did not support the planning proposal, finding it lacked strategic and site-specific merit. It also decided not to begin studies for a Northwood Heritage Conservation Area at this time.

76/2026.title: 2026/27 community assistance grants
76/2026.description: Council is allocating community grants, venue hire subsidies and recurring commitments for 2026/27.
76/2026.decisionSummary: Council approved $581,526 in grants and recurring commitments, including $520,922 for 15 recipients, and accepted the Historical Society's late application. It set conditions for any remaining funds granted to Lane Cove Public School, extended the Toy Library contract to June 2027 and approved an August presentation ceremony.

74/2026.title: Restricted cash reserves policy consultation
74/2026.description: The draft policy addresses money Council holds in restricted reserves.
74/2026.decisionSummary: Council approved the draft Restricted Cash Reserves Policy for public exhibition and requested a further report after consultation.

72/2026.title: 2–4 Pacific Highway planning agreement
72/2026.description: The planning agreement provides a monetary contribution for works at Wadanggari Park.
72/2026.decisionSummary: Council agreed to enter the planning agreement for 2–4 Pacific Highway, St Leonards. It specified that the monetary contribution would fund Wadanggari Park works and authorised completion of the documents.

70/2026.short: Backyard habitat for reptiles and small wildlife
70/2026.title: Backyard habitat for reptiles and small wildlife
70/2026.description: Council is investigating low-cost ways for residents to create habitat for native reptiles and other small wildlife.
70/2026.decisionSummary: Council requested a report on a low-cost urban habitat program using materials such as clay pipes, rocks and timber. The investigation is to consider costs, community participation, existing habitat programs and links to the Habitat Log Salvage proposal.

67/2026.short: 300 Burns Bay Road state development application
67/2026.title: 300 Burns Bay Road state development application
67/2026.description: Council is objecting to aspects of the state significant development proposal at 300 Burns Bay Road and seeking further public consultation.
67/2026.decisionSummary: Council agreed to request Independent Planning Commission determination, reopening of the exhibition period and at least 28 days' exhibition for state significant applications pending the new statewide plan. It also agreed to seek local MPs' support and noted its objection and public information webpage.

112/2026.title: NSW planning consultation rules submission
112/2026.description: Council is responding to proposed statewide rules for public notification and consultation on development.
112/2026.decisionSummary: Council endorsed a submission seeking longer exhibition periods for complex state significant applications, safeguards for notification of local developments, 14 days' notice before complying development works and longer consultation over Christmas. It authorised finalisation and submission to the planning department.

110/2026.title: 177–183 Greenwich Road planning proposal
110/2026.description: Planning Proposal 41 relates to land at 177–183 Greenwich Road, Greenwich.
110/2026.decisionSummary: Council endorsed Planning Proposal 41 and agreed to send it to the NSW planning department for finalisation. It authorised the General Manager to finalise the amendments.

108/2026.short: Organic Buyers Group community hub pilot
108/2026.title: Organic Buyers Group community hub pilot
108/2026.description: A proposed community hub would use a Council facility to support an Organic Buyers Group.
108/2026.decisionSummary: Council approved a 12-month pilot providing a suitable Council facility for up to two hours each week. It authorised an agreement covering operations and risk requirements, with a review after the pilot to decide its future.

106/2026.title: Planning agreements policy consultation
106/2026.description: Council is reviewing its policy for negotiating planning agreements, including agreements involving complying development.
106/2026.decisionSummary: Council authorised clarification of the draft policy's process for land subject to complying development applications. It agreed to six weeks' public exhibition and a report on the results.

102/2026.short: Library policies and events policy review
102/2026.title: Library policies and events policy review
102/2026.description: Council reviewed library service standards and a draft policy for managing events.
102/2026.decisionSummary: Council adopted the Library Policy and the service standards for library operations and collections. It agreed to exhibit the draft Events Management Policy for 28 days and receive a consultation report.

100/2026.title: March 2026 quarterly budget review
100/2026.description: Council reviewed its budget forecasts for the quarter ending March 2026.
100/2026.decisionSummary: Council approved revised forecasts: a $9.4 million operating surplus including capital grants and contributions, $42.3 million capital spending, a $960,000 net increase in transfers to and from reserves, and a balanced program budget.

98/2026.title: 2026/27 mayor and councillor fees
98/2026.description: Council is setting annual payments for the mayor and councillors from July 2026.
98/2026.decisionSummary: Council set the 2026/27 councillor fee at $24,080 a year and the additional mayoral fee at $52,520 a year, commencing on 1 July 2026.

96/2026.short: St Leonards South areas 22–23 agreement variation
96/2026.title: St Leonards South areas 22–23 agreement variation
96/2026.description: Council is consulting on a proposed change to the planning agreement for areas 22 and 23.
96/2026.decisionSummary: Council agreed to exhibit the proposed planning agreement variation and supporting documents for 28 days and receive a report on the results.

91/2026.short: Synthetic turf policy and private development rules
91/2026.title: Synthetic turf policy and private development rules
91/2026.description: Council is reviewing when synthetic turf should be used in public spaces and whether new private developments should face restrictions.
91/2026.decisionSummary: Council requested a draft policy favouring sustainable natural turf, with assessment and consultation requirements where synthetic turf is considered. It confirmed no intention to remove Blackman Park's existing turf and requested investigation of private development controls, natural alternatives and ways to improve sports field capacity.

88/2026.title: Recognising Jacky Barker's local journalism
88/2026.description: Council recognised Jacky Barker's contribution to local reporting and community information.
88/2026.decisionSummary: Council acknowledged Jacky Barker's contribution to Lane Cove and agreed to write thanking her for local journalism, promotion of local businesses, events and volunteering, and providing a platform for residents' views.

142/2026.title: May 2026 Local Transport Forum decisions
142/2026.description: Council considered the recommendations from the May Local Transport Forum meeting.
142/2026.decisionSummary: Council adopted the recommendations of the Local Transport Forum meeting held on 19 May 2026.

140/2026.short: Federal AI and data centres inquiry submission
140/2026.title: Federal AI and data centres inquiry submission
140/2026.description: Council is responding to a federal inquiry into artificial intelligence and data centres.
140/2026.decisionSummary: Council endorsed a submission calling for a pause on data centre approvals until planning rules address community and environmental concerns. It also called for new renewable energy infrastructure and stronger fire safety requirements, and authorised the General Manager to finalise the submission.

138/2026.title: Low-rise housing reforms submission
138/2026.description: Council is responding to proposed low-rise housing reforms and targeted assessment changes.
138/2026.decisionSummary: Council endorsed its submission on low-rise housing reforms and targeted assessment, and authorised the General Manager to finalise it for the NSW planning department.

136/2026.short: NSW children and young people plan submission
136/2026.title: NSW children and young people plan submission
136/2026.description: Council is responding to the proposed NSW Strategic Plan for Children and Young People 2027–2030.
136/2026.decisionSummary: Council endorsed its submission on the state plan and authorised it to be lodged with the NSW Office for Youth before 30 June 2026.

134/2026.short: Reserves and infrastructure asset policies adopted
134/2026.title: Reserves and infrastructure asset policies adopted
134/2026.description: Council reviewed consultation on its reserves and infrastructure asset management policies.
134/2026.decisionSummary: Council noted the consultation results and adopted the Internal Reserves Policy and Infrastructure Asset Management Policy. It required both documents to be published on its website.

132/2026.title: 2026/27 budget, rates and delivery program
132/2026.description: Council's annual package sets its budget, rates, fees, services and longer-term resources.
132/2026.decisionSummary: Council adopted the 2026/27 budget, rates and charges, delivery program, operational plan and resourcing documents after consultation. It also established a $135,000 reserve for minor capital works and required the Emergency Services Levy increase and other financial plan changes to be reflected in the published documents.

130/2026.title: Market Square centre manager procurement
130/2026.description: Council and Region Group are considering a centre manager for Market Square's shared building and facilities.
130/2026.decisionSummary: Council agreed to begin procuring a centre manager through the Building Management Committee, while noting Region Group intended to retain Knight Frank for its own operations. It requested performance measures and termination clauses for councillors to review before procurement begins.

128/2026.title: Advisory committee structure review
128/2026.description: Council is reviewing how advisory committees support communication between residents and Council.
128/2026.decisionSummary: Council requested a review with stakeholder consultation and a report by June 2027, followed by broader consultation and a feedback report by June 2028. Current committees and charters are to remain until the end of the Council term.

126/2026.title: Vacant development site maintenance
126/2026.description: Council is investigating how to require maintenance, revegetation and sediment controls on vacant development sites.
126/2026.decisionSummary: Council requested investigation of enforcement powers, recovery of Council costs, and consent conditions requiring maintenance, revegetation, sediment controls and a compliance bond. A report was requested for September 2026.

122/2026.title: Emergency Services Levy reform
122/2026.description: Council is responding to proposed changes in how NSW emergency services are funded.
122/2026.decisionSummary: Council supported removing the levy from insurance premiums and ending councils' contribution. It requested transparent modelling of land value impacts, supported Revenue NSW administration, opposed collection through Council rates and authorised a parliamentary submission and an LGNSW conference motion.

120/2026.title: 2026 King's Birthday Honours recipients
120/2026.description: Council recognised three Lane Cove residents named in the 2026 King's Birthday Honours.
120/2026.decisionSummary: Council acknowledged Professor William Rawlinson AC, Rod Cooke OAM and John Devine OAM. It agreed to write congratulating them and thanking them for their contributions.

166/2026.title: Market Square advertising management
166/2026.description: Council is reviewing who manages its advertising spaces at Market Square and how they should be used.
166/2026.decisionSummary: Council ended the Chamber of Commerce's role in obtaining advertisers and authorised transitional discussions. It requested a report on future management and whether commercial advertising should continue, with community and Council uses proposed if it does not.

164/2026.title: Small watercraft storage policy adopted
164/2026.description: The policy covers registration, storage locations and fees for small watercraft.
164/2026.decisionSummary: Council adopted the storage policy and map, affirmed the 2026/27 fees, and agreed to begin cleanup and registration at Griffith Park in Dunois Street, Woodford Bay. Further implementation depends on resources and budget, with sites listed on Council's website.

162/2026.title: Councillor code of conduct submission
162/2026.description: Council is responding to proposed changes to the model code of conduct for councillors.
162/2026.decisionSummary: Council endorsed its submission on the proposed model code and authorised it to be lodged with the Office of Local Government before 7 August 2026.

158/2026.title: Council risk management documents
158/2026.description: Council is reviewing its risk policy, management plan and statement of acceptable risk.
158/2026.decisionSummary: Council endorsed the revised Risk Management Policy and Enterprise Risk Management Plan, incorporating the Risk Appetite Statement.

156/2026.short: St Leonards South areas 22–23 variation approved
156/2026.title: St Leonards South areas 22–23 variation approved
156/2026.description: Council considered a change to the planning agreement for areas 22 and 23 after public exhibition.
156/2026.decisionSummary: Council agreed to enter the deed varying the planning agreement for areas 22 and 23 at St Leonards South. It authorised the General Manager to complete the necessary documents.

154/2026.short: Animal fur sales on Council land
154/2026.title: Animal fur sales on Council land
154/2026.description: Council is restricting animal fur sales at Council land, markets, events and community spaces, with specified exemptions.
154/2026.decisionSummary: Council prohibited animal fur sales in these locations, with exemptions including second-hand fur, art, taxidermy and Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander cultural practice. It requested updated rules, education-led enforcement, identification guidance, disposal information and advocacy for wider retail and import bans.

150/2026.short: More sporting facilities without losing green space
150/2026.title: More sporting facilities without losing green space
150/2026.description: Council is investigating ways to increase sporting capacity while protecting public green space, trees and biodiversity.
150/2026.decisionSummary: Council requested a review of sporting facility models, discussions about community access to school facilities, and investigation of planning incentives and agreements. A report is to identify local and regional opportunities and support advocacy for funding and policy changes.

197/2026.title: General Manager's 2025/26 performance review
197/2026.description: Council considered its performance panel's annual review of the General Manager.
197/2026.decisionSummary: Council endorsed the panel's Outstanding appraisal and recommended remuneration market adjustment in addition to the 3% award increase. It agreed to send the General Manager a written report of its conclusions.

192/2026.short: St Leonards Return and Earn investigation report
192/2026.title: St Leonards Return and Earn investigation report
192/2026.description: Council considered a report on possible Return and Earn container collection sites in St Leonards.
192/2026.decisionSummary: Council received and noted the report on the investigation into possible Return and Earn sites in St Leonards.

190/2026.title: Affordable housing policy adopted
190/2026.description: The policy sets Council's approach to affordable rental housing and priority tenants.
190/2026.decisionSummary: Council adopted the amended policy, including a target of at least 10% affordable rental housing in strategic plans and planning proposals, subject to demonstrated feasibility constraints. It also added people with a close connection to Lane Cove to the priority tenant list.

188/2026.title: Civic art collection policy adopted
188/2026.description: The policy sets how Council manages its civic art collection.
188/2026.decisionSummary: Council noted the public consultation results and adopted the amended Lane Cove Civic Art Collection Policy.

186/2026.title: Surveillance camera policy consultation
186/2026.description: Council is consulting on a policy for surveillance cameras.
186/2026.decisionSummary: Council agreed to publicly exhibit the draft Surveillance Camera Policy for at least 28 days and receive a report on the results.

184/2026.short: Support for people seeking asylum taskforce
184/2026.title: Support for people seeking asylum taskforce
184/2026.description: Council is reviewing its membership of a local government taskforce supporting people seeking asylum.
184/2026.decisionSummary: Council agreed to retain its Supporter Council membership of the Mayoral and Councillor Taskforce Supporting People Seeking Asylum.

182/2026.title: 2025/26 financial statements referred for audit
182/2026.description: Council's draft annual financial statements require external audit.
182/2026.decisionSummary: Council agreed to refer its draft general purpose financial statements for the year ending 30 June 2026 to the NSW Audit Office.

180/2026.title: June 2026 Audit Committee minutes
180/2026.description: Council considered draft minutes from its Audit, Risk and Improvement Committee.
180/2026.decisionSummary: Council noted the draft minutes of the committee's 30 June 2026 meeting and that they did not seek any action from Council.

177/2026.title: Temporary stalls in Wadanggari Park
177/2026.description: Council is investigating whether temporary street stalls could operate in designated parts of Wadanggari Park.
177/2026.decisionSummary: Council requested a report on suitable locations, safety and access conditions, permits, fees, consultation and an implementation timetable. It specified that any arrangements should provide equitable access under common approval criteria.

171/2026.title: NSW waste infrastructure planning advocacy
171/2026.description: Council is seeking a long-term state plan and planning changes for waste and recycling infrastructure.
171/2026.decisionSummary: Council agreed to request a 20-year NSW Waste and Circularity Infrastructure Roadmap and reforms to approval pathways. It called for collaboration with councils and industry and supported coordinated advocacy through Resilient Sydney and regional council organisations.

169/2026.title: Local school anniversary congratulations
169/2026.description: Council recognised major anniversaries for Lane Cove, Greenwich and Lane Cove West public schools.
169/2026.decisionSummary: Council congratulated Lane Cove and Greenwich public schools on their 150th anniversaries and Lane Cove West Public School on its 75th anniversary. It agreed to write to the principals and acknowledge the schools' contributions.

229/2026.short: Burns Bay Reserve masterplan further work
229/2026.title: Burns Bay Reserve masterplan further work
229/2026.description: Council is seeking changes to the remaining parts of the Burns Bay Reserve Masterplan.
229/2026.decisionSummary: Council deferred adoption pending expanded reserve boundaries, maintenance plans, a raised bike connection, more bike parking and creek-edge fencing. It also requested more detailed creek ecology and water-sensitive design proposals, linked to its earlier catchment planning resolution.

226/2026.title: Draft Bike Plan consultation
226/2026.description: Council's draft Bike Plan proposes a future cycling network and is being prepared for public consultation.
226/2026.decisionSummary: Council requested a Burns Bay Reserve route on RE1 land, use of the term Shared Spaces and correction of the future network length to 48.3 km. It agreed to six weeks' public exhibition and a report on the results.

224/2026.title: 3 Austin Crescent planning proposal
224/2026.description: Planning Proposal 47 relates to 3 Austin Crescent, Lane Cove.
224/2026.decisionSummary: Council endorsed Planning Proposal 47 and agreed to submit it to the NSW planning department for finalisation. It authorised the General Manager to finalise the amendments.

222/2026.title: DV Safe Phone collection arrangements
222/2026.description: Council has established a way to direct suitable donated phones from the Civic Centre to DV Safe Phone.
222/2026.decisionSummary: Council received the report and noted that a process had been established with the Reconnect Project to provide suitable phones collected at the Civic Centre directly to DV Safe Phone.

220/2026.title: Financial Assistance Grants allocation review
220/2026.description: Council is responding to proposed changes in how Financial Assistance Grants are distributed.
220/2026.decisionSummary: Council authorised a submission offering in-principle support for the proposed method while raising concern about potential revenue losses for Lane Cove. It also agreed to advocate through local government associations for a larger Commonwealth grant allocation.

218/2026.title: Local government performance ratios submission
218/2026.description: Council is responding to proposed performance measures for local government.
218/2026.decisionSummary: Council endorsed its submission on the Local Government Performance Ratios discussion paper and authorised it to be lodged with the Office of Local Government before 7 October 2026.

216/2026.title: Data breach response policy adopted
216/2026.description: The policy sets Council's response to a data breach.
216/2026.decisionSummary: Council adopted the Data Breach Response Policy and required it to be published on its website.

214/2026.title: Bushland protection development controls review
214/2026.description: Council is reviewing development controls for construction and buildings adjoining bushland.
214/2026.decisionSummary: Council requested a targeted review of Development Control Plan Part H, covering buffers, trees, excavation, runoff, construction, lighting, noise and compliance. Draft changes are to be discussed with advisory committees before returning to Council for public exhibition and consultation.

210/2026.title: 2026 volunteer award congratulations
210/2026.description: Council recognised Lane Cove residents and teams honoured in the NSW Volunteer of the Year Awards.
210/2026.decisionSummary: Council congratulated Gabriel Dickinson, Jeff Lewis and all recognised local residents and teams. It agreed to write to Dickinson and Lewis thanking them for their service and congratulating them on their awards.

203/2026.title: Councillor appointments to external organisations
203/2026.description: Council is appointing councillor representatives to external organisations for September 2026 to September 2028.
203/2026.decisionSummary: Council appointed representatives and alternates to Centrehouse, the retirement units association, NSROC, the NSW Public Libraries Association, Shorelink and the regional bushfire management committee until September 2028.

201/2026.title: Councillor appointments to advisory committees
201/2026.description: Council is appointing councillor representatives to its advisory committees for September 2026 to September 2028.
201/2026.decisionSummary: Council appointed councillor representatives and alternates to its advisory committees until September 2028, covering access and ageing, cycling, bushland, Carisbrook, companion animals, inclusion, festivals, public art, sport, sustainability and youth.

199/2026.title: Deputy Mayor election process
199/2026.description: Council is arranging the election of a deputy mayor for a one-year term.
199/2026.decisionSummary: Council agreed to conduct the Deputy Mayor election for a one-year term ending September 2027 under the Local Government General Regulation.
